IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference. IREN’s platform is underpinned by its expansive portfolio of grid-connected land and power in renewable-rich regions across North America, Europe and APAC.

The Engineering Manager is a critical leadership role within IREN’s Australian operations, responsible for leading and integrating a multidisciplinary engineering function that underpins the design, delivery, and operational performance of IREN’s large-scale, renewable-powered data centres. This role brings together deep technical expertise across electrical, high voltage, mechanical, civil/structural, controls, and asset management disciplines to ensure IREN’s Australian data centre portfolio is delivered and operated safely, sustainably, and to the highest standard.

With 100% renewable energy, we build, own and operate our data centers and take pride in being at the forefront of sustainable solutions for the ever-evolving applications of high-performance compute. We believe that human progress is invaluable, but it should be done in the right way – responsibly, sustainably and having a positive impact on the communities we operate in.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Mechanical, or Civil/Structural Engineering, or a related engineering discipline. A Master’s degree is advantageous.
  • Registration as a Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) with Engineers Australia, or eligibility and commitment to attain registration within an agreed time frame.
  • 15+ years of progressive engineering experience, including significant time leading multidisciplinary engineering teams on large-scale capital projects in mission-critical, industrial, or infrastructure environments.
  • Demonstrated experience in data centre, energy, utilities, or heavy infrastructure sectors, with familiarity across electrical (HV/MV/LV), mechanical, civil/structural, controls, and commissioning scopes.
  • Strong understanding of Australian standards and regulatory frameworks applicable to data centres and critical infrastructure, including AS/NZS standards, NCC (National Construction Code), WHS legislation, and state-specific electrical and building codes.
  • Proven ability to lead, mentor, and develop senior engineers and technical leads across multiple disciplines simultaneously.
  • Experience managing engineering delivery through EPC contractors, specialist consultants, and OEM vendors, including technical review, governance, and risk management.
  • Familiarity with asset management principles, DCIM tools, building automation systems (BAS), and data centre infrastructure management; experience with CMMS platforms is desirable.
  • Strong understanding of commissioning methodologies, FAT/SAT processes, energization readiness, and structured handover to operations.
  • Demonstrated capability in technical risk identification, change management, and executive-level reporting across complex, multi-stakeholder programs.
  • Excellent leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to engage effectively with executive leadership, contractors, regulators, and community stakeholders.
  • Self-driven, highly organised, and capable of managing competing priorities across multiple concurrent workstreams in a fast-paced, growth-oriented environment.
  • Flexible approach to working hours to support IREN’s multi-time-zone, global operations; willingness to travel to Australian site locations and, occasionally, internationally as required.

Responsibilities

  • Provide strategic technical leadership across all engineering disciplines, including electrical, high voltage, mechanical, civil/structural, controls, and commissioning functions, ensuring integrated and coordinated delivery of IREN’s Australian data centre projects.
  • Directly manage and develop a multidisciplinary team of senior engineers and leads, including the Senior Electrical Engineer, HV Design Lead, Power Systems Lead, Electrical Design Lead, Mechanical Lead, Civil/Structural Lead, Controls Lead, Asset Manager, and Commissioning Manager.
  • Serve as the primary technical authority for engineering decisions across capital projects and operational initiatives in Australia, ensuring designs and workscomply withAustralian standards, codes, and regulatory requirements (including AS/NZS standards, NCC, and state-specific requirements).
  • Oversee the review, approval, and governance of all engineering deliverables, drawings, specifications, and technical submissions produced internally or by external consultants, EPC contractors, and vendors.

  • Manage vendor and EPC relationships from a technical perspective; support bid evaluations, technical clarifications, and contractor selection to ensure compliance with IREN standards and project requirements.
  • Oversee factory acceptance testing (FAT), site acceptance testing (SAT), commissioning readiness, and safe energisation across all systems, ensuring structured handover to operations.
  • Drive standardisation of engineering approaches across the Australian portfolio, capturing lessons learned and embedding them into future project delivery.
  • Partner with the VP – Operations Australia and cross-functional teams including construction, procurement, and asset management to align engineering outcomes with broader businessobjectives.
  • Ensure all engineering activitiescomply withWork Health and Safety (WHS) legislation and IREN’s safety management requirements, championing a zero-harm culture across the engineering function.
  • Support asset lifecycle management, maintenance planning, and operational reliability in close collaboration with the Asset Manager and Commissioning Manager.
  • Mentor and develop engineering team members, fostering a high-performance culture built on technical excellence, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

job.title: High Voltage Design Lead
job.description:
About the Role

Job Type: Full-time | Location: Sydney, Australia | Department: Engineering | Reporting to: Engineering Manager |Work Location: #Hybrid

IREN is a vertically integrated AI Cloud provider, delivering large-scale data centers and GPU clusters for AI training and inference. IREN’s platform is underpinned by its expansive portfolio of grid-connected land and power in renewable-rich regions across North America, Europe and APAC.

As the High Voltage Design Lead at IREN, you will own and drive the high voltage (HV) electrical scope that enables reliable, utility-scale power delivery to our AI data centers. You will lead the development of HV concepts and standards, manage utility and interconnection interfaces, and provide technical leadership from early-stage site power strategy through detailed design, construction, testing, and commissioning. This role is hands-on and highly cross-functional, partnering with development, construction, commissioning, and operations to deliver safe, scalable, and cost-effective grid connections and HV infrastructure.

With 100% renewable energy, we build, own and operate our data centers and take pride in being at the forefront of sustainable solutions for the ever-evolving applications of high-performance compute. We believe that human progress is invaluable, but it should be done in the right way – responsibly, sustainably and having a positive impact on the communities we operate in.

Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering from an accredited institution (Master’s degree is an asset).
  • 8+ years of progressive experience delivering HV/MV power systems, substations/switchyards, and/or utility interconnections for mission-critical, industrial, or utility-scale projects.
  • Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) with Engineers Australia, or eligibility and commitment to attain CPEng registration within an agreed time frame.
  • Strong knowledge of HV equipment and systems: power transformers, breakers, disconnect switches, instrument transformers (CTs/VTs), bus, surge arresters, earthing systems, and cable/line interfaces.
  • Experience with protection & control systems including relay schemes, metering, SCADA/communications, and commissioning/testing workflows (e.g., secondary injection, end-to-end testing).
  • Working knowledge of applicable standards and codes such as AS/NZS 3000, AS 2067 (substations), IEC 61936, IEC 60909, IEEE, and relevant DNSP/NSP technical standards and connection requirements; familiarity with AEMO grid connection processes and the National Electricity Rules (NER) is highly desirable.
  • Proven ability to lead technical scope across multiple stakeholders (utilities, EPCs, OEMs, network service providers (NSPs/DNSPs), state electrical safety regulators, and local councils) with strong documentation, communication, and decision-making skills.

Responsibilities

Reporting to the Engineering Manager, the High Voltage Design Lead will lead and deliver HV electrical strategy, design oversight, and technical execution for IREN’s AI data center developments. You will ensure safety, reliability, schedule certainty, and compliance across utility interconnection, substations/switchyards, HV equipment, and related protection and control systems.

  • Lead HV power delivery strategy for new and expanding AI datacenters, including utility engagement, capacity planning, phasing, redundancy concepts, and constructability inputs.
  • Own utility and grid interconnection interfaces: coordinate technical requirements, review interconnection studies, manage data requests, and align designs with utility standards and project schedules.
  • Develop and review HV/MV system designs (typical 12kV–230kV, project-dependent) including substations/switchyards, transformers, breakers, disconnects, bus work, grounding grids, duct banks, overhead/underground feeders, and station service.
  • Lead protection and control (P&C) technical scope: relay philosophy, protection coordination inputs, metering, SCADA/telemetry, settings review, and end-to-end testing strategy with commissioning teams.
  • Provide technical leadership through design and construction: review drawings and specifications, resolve RFIs, support field execution, and ensure safe installation practices and quality documentation for turnover.
  • Manage vendor/EPC deliverables and technical risk: evaluate equipment and contractor proposals, drive clarity on scope boundaries, and ensure compliance with IREN standards, applicable codes, and utility requirements.
  • Plan and support factory and site testing (FAT/SAT), energization readiness, and commissioning activities; troubleshoot issues, implement corrective actions, and support safe return-to-service.
  • Drive standardization across IREN’s HV program: develop templates, basis-of-design, typical one-lines, grounding and P&C philosophies, and lessons learned to accelerate repeatable delivery.

Benefits

At IREN, we offer a comprehensive, market-competitive total rewards package designed to support employees’ well-being, career advancement, and financial wealth. Our offerings reflect our commitment to Proceed with Purpose while rewarding high performance and long-term growth.

  • Compensation & Rewards

Competitive salary range based on experience and impact Short- and long-term incentive programs designed to reward both results and long term company success

Wellbeing & Benefits

  • Comprehensive extended health and dental coverage to keep you and your family supported
  • Three weeks of paid vacation to recharge, travel, or simply enjoy more life outside of work (note that paid vacation is for salaried employees only)

Work Environment A modern hybrid model — collaborate in our Sydney office Tuesday–Thursday, with flexibility the rest of the week Casual, comfortable attire so you can bring your best self to work without the suit-and-tie Access to an onsite, fully equipped gym to make wellness part of your workday

We value diverse perspectives and believe that skills can be developed. If you’re passionate about this role, we want to hear from you — whether you meet every criteria or not. Your unique experiences might be exactly what we need! IREN is an equal opportunity employer that is committed to creating an inclusive workplace. We are committed to evaluating qualified applicants and do not discriminate against protected characteristics under applicable legislation. This job will remain posted until filled. While we appreciate all applications we receive, we are only able to contact candidates under consideration. By applying for this position and submitting your resume and application materials, you consent to the processing of your personal information in accordance with our Job Applicant Privacy Statement available on our website at www.iren.com. ​

Manufacturing Engineering Manager__

Your role and responsibilities

In this role, you will support maintenance activities necessary to achieve the required level of quality, costs and production capacity for active products. You will work closely with wider R&D and Agile teams for technical input, while maintaining strong communication with Supply Chain Management (SCM) and Production teams. You will also have the exciting opportunity to contribute to new product developments, including assembling prototypes and testing new designs — making this a fantastic role for a graduate looking to build broad engineering experience in a growing, global business.

Work model: #onsite in Napier #LI-Onsite

  • Establishing project specifications for production
  • Converting R&D developments into products for market and readying these for mass production
  • Problem solving analysis and investigation together with Quality and Process teams

You will join a talented, collaborative team that values innovation and continuous learning. job.title: Lead DNS Engineer
job.description:
About the role

Optus is seeking a Lead DNS Engineer to provide hands-on technical leadership across our carrier-grade DNS environment.

This is a DNS-first senior individual contributor role responsible for the technical integrity, design, and implementation of DNS services across authoritative DNS, resolver DNS, cache DNS, DNS security controls, observability, and lifecycle uplift.

The successful candidate will operate as the senior engineering lead for DNS, combining architecture and standards with practical implementation. This role is expected to design solutions, build and improve configurations and automation, lead complex technical change, and materially reduce service risk across current and future DNS platforms.

The position is for an engineer who can move between strategy and execution — someone who can define the right design and then help implement it in production.

**

What You’ll Do

**

DNS architecture, design, and implementation

  • Design and implement solutions across authoritative DNS, recursive DNS, cache DNS, DNS policy services, and DNS control plane functions.
  • Define and maintain target-state architecture and engineering patterns for Consumer, Enterprise, and Internal DNS services.
  • Produce practical designs that can be implemented safely in production, including migration patterns, coexistence models, failover design, and rollback strategy.
  • Build and improve DNS configurations, service patterns, and deployment approaches across current and future DNS platforms.

DNS platform engineering and change delivery

  • Lead hands-on implementation of complex DNS changes, upgrades, migrations, and resilience improvements.
  • Improve DNS automation, validation, and deployment workflows to reduce manual risk and increase repeatability.
  • Work through deep technical details of zone management, zone publication, policy distribution, hidden master operation, and service cutover.
  • Support and technically lead platform transition programs, ensuring design intent is carried through into implementation.

Lifecycle uplift and technical risk reduction

  • Identify DNS lifecycle exposure across software, supporting components, and service dependencies, and drive practical remediation plans.
  • Reduce technical debt and simplify brittle service patterns through engineering change, not just documentation.
  • Improve service resilience, recovery readiness, and observability through targeted implementation work and design correction.
  • Support technology refresh and service modernisation by taking designs through to deployable outcomes.

DNS security, service correctness, and resilience

  • Design and implement improvements to DNS security controls including DNSSEC, TSIG, access control, RPZ policy handling, secure administration, and auditability.
  • Improve service correctness across authoritative, resolver, and cache paths, including failover behaviour, propagation behaviour, and dependency management.
  • Define and implement guardrails for safe DNS change, including validation, rollback expectations, and production-readiness checks.
  • Support major incidents, root cause analysis, and recurring issue elimination with a strong engineering focus on prevention.

Engineering leadership and cross-functional execution

  • Work closely with platform engineering, network engineering, security, operations, and vendor teams to turn DNS service requirements into deployable and supportable solutions.
  • Provide senior technical leadership during design, implementation, and stabilisation of DNS changes.
  • Improve engineering documentation, build standards, implementation patterns, runbooks, and migration artefacts.
  • Mentor engineers and contribute to lifting practical DNS engineering capability across the organisation.

**

What makes you the right fit for the role?

  • Deep hands-on expertise in DNS engineering across authoritative DNS, recursive DNS, cache DNS, and DNS service operations.
  • Strong understanding of DNS protocols, record types, zone design, split-horizon or split-view DNS, recursion behaviour, forwarding, and cache behaviour.
  • Proven experience designing and implementing production DNS services in large-scale enterprise, ISP, carrier, or service provider environments.
  • Strong knowledge of DNS security concepts including DNSSEC, TSIG, response policy mechanisms, access control, and service hardening.
  • Experience implementing resilient DNS designs including hidden masters, secondaries, anycast-based service delivery, failover patterns, and control/data plane separation.
  • Strong problem-solving capability across complex service incidents, technical debt, lifecycle uplift, and architectural remediation.
  • Experience building or improving DNS automation, validation, deployment, or migration workflows.
  • Experience producing high-quality engineering documentation such as design documents, standards, runbooks, migration plans, and risk assessments.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex DNS concepts to engineering operations, architecture, and leadership audiences.

Leadership attributes

  • Strong engineering judgement
  • Structured and pragmatic problem solving
  • Ownership mindset for service quality and technical integrity
  • Ability to balance immediate operational realities with long-term design direction
  • Calm, credible presence during major incidents and critical changes
  • Collaborative approach across service, platform, and operations teams

**

Essential experience and capability

  • Deep hands-on expertise in DNS engineering across authoritative DNS, recursive DNS, cache DNS, and DNS service operations.
  • Strong understanding of DNS protocols, record types, zone design, split-horizon or split-view DNS, recursion behaviour, forwarding, and cache behaviour.
  • Proven experience designing and implementing production DNS services in large-scale enterprise, ISP, carrier, or service provider environments.
  • Strong knowledge of DNS security concepts including DNSSEC, TSIG, response policy mechanisms, access control, and service hardening.
  • Experience implementing resilient DNS designs including hidden masters, secondaries, anycast-based service delivery, failover patterns, and control/data plane separation.
  • Strong problem-solving capability across complex service incidents, technical debt, lifecycle uplift, and architectural remediation.
  • Experience building or improving DNS automation, validation, deployment, or migration workflows.
  • Experience producing high-quality engineering documentation such as design documents, standards, runbooks, migration plans, and risk assessments.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to explain complex DNS concepts to engineering operations, architecture, and leadership audiences.

Desirable experience and capability

  • Strong systems and platform engineering capability across Linux-based infrastructure, service hardening, observability, and lifecycle management.
  • Working knowledge of server, OS, virtualisation, and platform operations relevant to carrier-grade DNS environments.
  • Familiarity with network and traffic engineering constructs such as BGP anycast, load balancing, routing daemons, HA clustering, and service advertisement models.
  • Experience with DNS platforms and products such as BIND, Unbound, Power DNS, F5 BIG-IP DNS or similar.
  • Exposure to automation and infrastructure tooling used to manage DNS at scale, including APIs, scripting, CI/CD, infrastructure-as-code, configuration management, and service onboarding workflows.
  • Experience with service observability platforms, telemetry pipelines, logging, SNMP-based monitoring, and performance analysis.
  • Experience working in regulated or highly available production environments where uptime, auditability, and service correctness are critical.
  • Ability to work effectively with platform, infrastructure, and operations teams to translate service requirements into deployable runtime patterns.

**

The good stuff….

  • Competitive remuneration and colleague discounts. Make life easier (and more affordable) with $80 monthly credit and 25% off Optus products and outstanding shopping discounts with our retail partners.
  • Flexible working arrangements with opportunities to work three days in the office, two days remote or home.
  • Vibrant and collaborative office campus that includes cafes, a convenience store, chill-out zones, GP, post office, gym, and on-site childcare centre.
  • Competitive leave policies, including additional 'Connected’ days to focus on culture, family, health, community, or whatever’s important to you.
  • We support growing families with inclusive, carer-neutral paid Parental Leave of up to 16 weeks.
  • Build meaningful connections through colleague-led networks and diversity initiatives including Culture Connect, Elevate Women, Disability Network, and Express Yourself (LGBTQIA+).
  • Put your wellbeing first with free access to counselling and support services, 24/7 — in-person, by phone, SMS, or video.
  • Free Optus bus from Macquarie University Metro Station (every 6-8 minutes); morning and afternoon.

At Optus, we are strengthened by others and that means valuing diversity and saying ‘yes’ to embracing individual differences. We are committed to ensuring that our application process provides an equal employment opportunity to all job seekers, including individuals from diverse gender, cultural and linguistic backgrounds, individuals with a disability, individuals identifying as being part of the LGBTQIA+ community, individuals who may have served in the armed forces or who identify as Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander. We also want to do our best to make our recruitment process inclusive. If you require any adjustments or accessibility support to participate fairly and equitably in the recruitment process, please email [AccessibleRecruitment@optus.com.au](mailto:accessiblerecruitment@optus.com.au) or call 1800 309 170.

For more information on Diversity, Inclusion & Belonging at Optus, please visit [https://www.optus.com.au/about/inclusion-diversity](https://www.optus.com.au/about/inclusion-diversity)

job.title: Community and Social Impact Manager
job.description:
About us

Established in 2007, CDC Data Centres is Australia's leading operator of sovereign, secure, world-class data centre facilities.

Headquartered in Canberra with multiple facilities in the ACT, NSW, VIC and New Zealand, CDC's diversified operations provide secure data centre configurations that support co-location, containerised and hyperscale compute environments with all campuses interconnected with high-speed carrier grade networks.

At CDC we are passionate about creating an inclusive workplace that promotes and values diversity. We believe that everyone's unique experiences enable us to deliver meaningful benefits for our people, our clients and communities. Our mission is to attract, retain and grow the world's best data centre team.

Our people are committed, tenacious and meticulous in supporting our customers. Together, we configure the landscape to meet the security, reliability, connectivity and sustainability needs for today and tomorrow.

About the Role

The Community Engagement Specialist is CDC’s on-the-ground presence across metropolitan and regional areas. The role supports the relationship between CDC and the communities that host our campuses through planning, approvals, construction and operations.

Responsibilities

  • Act as CDC’s local, visible point of contact for host communities across metropolitan and regional areas, building trusted relationships with residents, community groups, councils, Traditional Owners, elected representatives and local stakeholders.
  • Run listening, consultation and two-way feedback in line with the IAP2 spectrum, using a closed-loop system that captures concerns, acts on them and shows communities what changed through ‘you said, we did’ updates.
  • Gather community intelligence through direct engagement, local media and social monitoring, council-minute scanning and surveys, and feed it into CDC’s traffic-light sentiment view.
  • - Contribute frontline insight to CDC’s community engagement strategy, standards, tools and assurance, keeping the enterprise approach practical and grounded in community experience.
  • Help build and continuously improve CDC’s repeatable engagement and benefit-sharing approach so each new site starts from proven practice.

What's in it for you:

CDC offers excellent employment conditions and benefits such as:

  • CDC Academy -Make your mark by enhancing your professional development with the CDC Academy. Enrol in specialised training courses that will help you develop skills and ensure you thrive in your chosen career.
  • CDC Day - An additional day of paid leave dedicated to nurturing your health and wellbeing.
  • Parental Leave - Inclusive and above legislative tenure of parental leave entitlements to help you start, grow and care for your family.
  • Volunteer Leave - Make a meaningful difference with 2 days of volunteering leave for any cause or charity of your choice.
  • Employment Assistance Program - Be confident that you and your family are supported with access to our comprehensive Employee Assistance Program.
  • CDC Social Events - CDC's offers staff and their family's inclusive events that nurtures relationships, connection and friendships across the business. CDC hosts BBQs, family picnics and community events, bringing together CDC staff in different settings.

About You

  • 5+ years’ experience in community engagement, stakeholder relations, social impact or external affairs, including hands-on delivery in host communities.
  • Experience delivering community or stakeholder engagement for major projects in infrastructure, property, energy, utilities, renewables or another complex, asset-intensive or regulated sector.
  • Practical command of engagement practice and frameworks such as the IAP2 spectrum, consultation, complaints handling and closed-loop feedback.
  • Understanding of the planning and approvals environment and how community sentiment affects development application and consenting outcomes.
  • Experience working alongside delivery partners and agencies to deliver local engagement.
  • A current driver’s licence and willingness to travel and work across metropolitan and regional areas, including occasional after-hours community events.

Essential: Australian Citizenship with ability to obtain and maintain a NV1 Security Clearance.

How to Apply:

If you are looking for an opportunity to play a vital role in a fast-growing Australian Technology company and be part of our amazing team, please submit your resume and cover letter by clicking Apply.

We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive workplace where all individuals are valued and respected. We believe that diversity of backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences leads to innovation and success. We actively promote equality and strive to create a welcoming environment for all employees. We are dedicated to building a team that reflects the diversity of our community and encourages everyone to bring their authentic selves to work.

job.title: ID - Rack Lifecycle Tech , Rack Lifecycle Team
job.description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Job Summary

We are looking for a detail-oriented, technically skilled Rack Lifecycle Tech to join our Rack Lifecycle Team within AWS Infrastructure Operations. In this individual contributor role, you will be a hands-on executor responsible for the physical installation, cabling, handoff, and decommissioning of racks across your assigned data center site. You are the person on the floor who turns capacity plans into operational reality.

As a Rack Lifecycle Tech, you will execute structured cabling, rack installation, and decommission activities with precision and to standard — following established SOPs, escalating deviations to your team lead, and ensuring every rack you touch is installed correctly, cabled to specification, fully documented, and handed off with zero blockers. This is an individual contributor role with no people management responsibilities. Your work is foundational to AWS’s ability to deliver infrastructure capacity to customers reliably, safely, and at the lowest possible cost.

Key job responsibilities 🔷 Rack Installation & Cabling

  • Execute rack installations including physical placement, power connections, grounding, and cable management per AWS standards and MOPs
  • Perform structured cabling including fiber/copper terminations, patch panel connections, labeling, and dressing to specification
  • Complete OTDR and power testing; validate results against acceptance thresholds; escalate failures to team lead promptly rather than self-resolving outside approved procedures
  • Follow all EHS protocols, lockout/tagout (LOTO) procedures, and safe work practices during installation activities

🔷 Rack Lifecycle Operations

  • Execute work orders and tasks assigned by the Rack Lifecycle Team Manager under direct manager direction, maintaining accurate status updates in workflow management tools (e.g., Boost, MARS)
  • Perform quality checks on completed cabling work including port map verification, label accuracy, and as-built documentation updates in CMDB/DCIM
  • Identify and escalate issues, blockers, or deviations from SOPs encountered during task execution to the team lead or manager promptly; do not self-resolve outside approved procedures
  • Support deployment wave readiness by participating in pre-work site walks, material staging, and tool preparation

🔷 Material Handling & Supply Chain Support

  • Receive, verify, and stage incoming rack, cable, optics, and hardware deliveries; validate against BOM and flag discrepancies
  • Maintain accurate site inventory records for cables, optics, patch cords, and consumables used during deployments
  • Support cycle count activities and assist in identifying inventory shortfalls that may impact deployment timelines

🔷 Handover & Documentation

  • Complete all required as-built documentation, port maps, test result records, and workflow sign-offs before handoff to Data Center Operations
  • Update CMDB/DCIM and IPAM records accurately following rack installation or decommission activities
  • Ensure handoffs are clean and fully documented with zero open blockers, enabling smooth transition to the next lifecycle phase

🔷 Rack Decommissioning

  • Execute physical decommission activities per assigned MOPs — including cable removal, power disconnects, asset de-tagging, and rack extraction
  • Perform device wipe and media destruction in compliance with AWS Secure Media Destruction and EHS policies
  • Sort, label, and stage recovered assets (optics, cables, PDUs, hardware) for RMA, redeployment, or secure disposal per AWS Reverse Logistics policy
  • Update DCIM/CMDB, IPAM, and port maps post-decom to ensure accurate space, power, and circuit records
  • Validate that reclaimed U-space, power, and cooling capacity is accurately recorded in the available pool

🔷 Quality, Safety & Compliance

  • Adhere to all site-level SOPs, quality standards, and governance frameworks for cabling, installation, and decommission activities
  • Complete all required safety training and certifications; participate in regular EHS audits and team safety briefings
  • Contribute to continuous improvement by identifying recurring quality issues, suggesting process improvements, and sharing feedback with the Rack Lifecycle Team Manager
  • Use Rack Lifecycle Team tooling (e.g., Boost, MARS, ALM/DCLM) accurately to record work, track assets, and maintain data integrity

🔷 Cross-Team Coordination

  • Support coordination with DCO, DCEO, Network Engineering, and facilities teams during active deployment or decom activities under manager guidance to ensure smooth execution
  • Participate in daily stand-ups and pre-work briefings; communicate clearly on task status, blockers, and schedule adherence
  • Provide accurate, timely updates on task completion and flag risks or delays to the team lead immediately

🔷 Continuous Learning & Development

  • Maintain and develop technical proficiency in structured cabling, fiber optics, rack installation, and data center physical infrastructure
  • Complete required certifications and training modules including EHS, LOTO, and any Rack Lifecycle Team-specific technical programs
  • Proactively seek feedback from leads and managers to improve personal performance and output quality
  • Support the onboarding and training of new team members; share knowledge and best practices with peers to build overall team capability and quality standards
  • Stay current on AWS infrastructure tooling, cabling standards, and process updates communicated by the Rack Lifecycle Team

A day in the life As a Rack Lifecycle Tech, your day is on the data center floor. You might start the morning by reviewing your assigned work orders in Boost, checking in with your team lead on priorities, and staging cables and optics for a rack installation wave. By midday, you could be terminating fiber runs at a patch panel, running OTDR tests to validate loss results against acceptance thresholds, or labeling and dressing a freshly installed rack. In the afternoon, you might be updating CMDB records for completed work orders, de-tagging and staging recovered assets from an EOL decom, or helping onboard a new technician by walking them through the SOP. If you encounter a deviation from the approved MOP, you escalate it to your team lead immediately — you don't improvise. Your role is hands-on, technical, and precise — you execute the work that keeps AWS capacity on track.

About the team Diverse Experiences Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Inclusive Team Culture AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship and Career Growth We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic Qualifications

  • 2+ years of computer hardware troubleshooting and repair experience
  • 1+ years of computer networking experience
  • High school or equivalent diploma

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience dealing effectively with customers during problem resolution and operating efficiently under pressure
  • Familiarity with rack decommissioning including device wipe, media destruction, and asset recovery procedures

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit [https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations](https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations) for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

job.title: Senior Security Solution Architect, APJC Customer Security, APJC Customer Security
job.description:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is seeking a Senior Secure AI Solution Architect to join our APJC Customer Security team. This is a builder's role. Customers across the region are moving fast on AI and seeking guidance on challenges they have not faced before — how to give autonomous agents an identity, how to defend against prompt injection, how to govern the AI development lifecycle, and how to produce the governance evidence a regulator will trust. You are the architect who helps them get there, working hands-on in their environment to build the prototypes and proofs of concept that turn ambition into validated proof — often in days.

You operate at the frontier, where the path forward is still being defined. Customers have a clear objective: put agentic AI into production while managing risk, regulatory, and data-residency obligations. Your role is to design the way there — creating new approaches where no established pattern exists and applying judgment about each customer's operational context and regulatory environment. You are technically self-sufficient: you write the code, deploy it with IaC, harden it, and demonstrate it live against real data.

Depth alone is not the job — scale is. The hardest problems you solve with one customer should lift the whole field. You independently dive deep on complex, novel Secure AI challenges, produce original technical content (reference architectures, working code, patterns, workshops), and share it so a pattern proven with one customer becomes something every area can reuse. You own the relationship with AWS service teams (Bedrock, AgentCore, SageMaker) — you are the voice of the field that shapes the product roadmap, and the voice of the product that shapes field guidance.

Security and governance are what let customers say yes to AI with confidence. You give the CISO the frameworks, evidence, and tooling to move quickly and safely, and you give the CIO/CTO confidence that governance won't slow delivery. You are the proof that AWS is the best place to build securely with AI.

Key job responsibilities Key job responsibilities

  • Build working prototypes and proofs of concept in customer sandbox environments — using AWS AI services (Bedrock, AgentCore, SageMaker), AI-augmented development tooling, and IaC (CDK, Terraform) — that prove a Secure AI control works against the customer's data and risk model, in days rather than quarters.
  • Implement directly to unblock decisions: stand up agentic-identity, prompt-injection-defence, AI development lifecycle, guardrail, and audit/evidence patterns that validate what conversations alone cannot.
  • Stay engaged through implementation so the design holds against reality; exercise judgment on when to revise the approach based on what you learn.

Partner with the Bedrock, AgentCore, and SageMaker service teams — you are the voice of APJC field security requirements that shapes what ships, and the voice of the product that shapes what the field advises.

  • Feed customer voices back through feature requests and direct engagement, staying current with a threat and regulatory landscape that moves in hours.
  • Translate service-team roadmap into field-ready guidance, ensuring it gets packaged at scale.
  • Produce original technical content — reference architectures, working code, patterns, blog posts, and workshops — that peers and customers adopt, turning a single customer win into reusable regional IP.
  • Mentor and develop others — area-based Solutions Architects and the wider field community — raising the Secure AI technical bar across the region and growing the next set of specialists.
  • Hand proven patterns to the content and enablement team so guidance reaches the field without requiring your presence.

A day in the life You start the morning in a customer's sandbox, not a slide deck. A financial-services customer wants to launch an agentic application on Bedrock, and overnight the identity and audit controls you built produced exactly the evidence their CISO needed. You tidy the code, capture the pattern, and prep a short summary naming the two guardrail settings that gave them confidence to proceed.

Mid-morning you join your Security Sales partner and the area account team with a manufacturer who wants to build with Bedrock and needs guidance on governing data residency and PII. It is a genuinely new problem — no established pattern exists — so you design the way forward: you whiteboard an agentic-identity and data-residency approach, then commit to prototyping the non-human-identity pattern their builder team will adopt.

After lunch you go heads-down and build it — hands on keyboard, deploying to a sandbox, hardening it — then run a working session with a customer's platform team on prompt-injection defence for a coding-assistant rollout.

You close the day scaling beyond yourself: you package this week's FSI win into a reference architecture the other areas can reuse, hand it to the content team to turn into a workshop, share a write-up with the field, and file a feature request for the AgentCore team based on what you learned. No two days look the same, but the thread is consistent: you help a customer accelerate securely, then turn what you built into something the whole region benefits from.

About the team APJC Customer Security helps customers across the region adopt AI on AWS with confidence — ensuring security, risk, and regulation accelerate AI adoption rather than slow it down. We run two coupled programmes: Secure AI (making AWS the best place to build securely with AI) and AI for Security (using AI to help customers defend themselves). As a Senior Secure AI Solution Architect, you are the deep technical expertise brought directly to where customers need it. You define the approach on novel problems, prove it hands-on, then hand the pattern to the content team and the field to scale. You will have a clear development path, a peer community of specialists, direct leadership visibility, and the autonomy to set technical direction in one of the most consequential areas in the industry.

Basic Qualifications

  • 8+ years of specific technology domain areas (e.g. software development, cloud computing, systems engineering, infrastructure, security, networking, data & analytics) experience
  • 3+ years of design, implementation, or consulting in applications and infrastructures experience
  • 10+ years of IT development or implementation/consulting in the software or Internet industries experience

Preferred Qualifications

  • 5+ years of infrastructure architecture, database architecture and networking experience
  • Experience within specific technology domain areas (e.g. software development, cloud computing, systems engineering, infrastructure, security, networking, data & analytics).
  • Knowledge and skills in Securing Generative AI Applications

job.title: Senior Product Manager
job.description:
Job Summary

The Product Manager will partner with the Tax business and technology teams to define, develop, and manage the lifecycle of Tax Technology products and solutions from discovery through delivery, adoption, and continuous improvement.

The role will translate Tax business needs and pain points into a clear product strategy, roadmap, and prioritized product capabilities, working closely with engineering, data, technology, and global Tax stakeholders.

The ideal candidate combines strong Tax domain expertise, product management capability, technology understanding, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to operate across business and technical teams.

###

Key Responsibilities

Product Roadmap

  • ### Partner with Tax stakeholders to understand business priorities, processes, pain points, and technology opportunities.
  • ### Define and prioritize the Tax Technology product roadmap aligned with business and IT strategy.
  • ### Identify opportunities to simplify, automate, and improve Tax processes through technology and data products.
  • ### Balance business value, technical feasibility, risk, scalability, and delivery priorities.

Product Discovery & Requirements

  • ### Translate Tax business requirements into product capabilities, user stories, and prioritized backlog items.
  • ### Understand end-to-end Tax processes and data flows across Oracle Financials, Oracle TRCS, transfer pricing and related systems.
  • ### Partner with Tax users to identify opportunities for automation, analytics, reconciliation, and improved decision-making.
  • ### Evaluate business needs and define solutions that can scale across global Tax teams.

Product Development & Delivery

  • ### Own product development from discovery and requirements through delivery, UAT, launch, adoption, and continuous improvement.
  • ### Partner with engineering, data, and technology teams to define product requirements and delivery priorities.
  • ### Lead backlog refinement, prioritization, dependency management, and release planning.
  • ### Define acceptance criteria, test cases, and UAT requirements to ensure solutions meet business outcomes.
  • ### Monitor product adoption, quality, performance, and user feedback and drive continuous improvements.

Business Value & Stakeholder Management

  • ### Build business cases and articulate the value, ROI, and business impact of product investments.
  • ### Define success metrics such as adoption, automation, efficiency, reporting cycle time, data quality, and user experience.
  • ### Build strong relationships with global Tax stakeholders and manage expectations across business and technology teams.
  • ### Communicate product strategy, roadmap, priorities, risks, and progress to senior stakeholders.

Market & Product Innovation

  • ### Stay current on emerging Tax Technology, AI, automation, analytics
  • ### Evaluate industry solutions and identify opportunities to improve the Tax technology ecosystem.
  • ### Recommend product enhancements and new capabilities based on business needs and market trends.

###

Qualifications

  • ### 8+ years of experience in Product Management, Product Ownership, Business Systems, Technology Consulting, or Functional Consulting.
  • ### Strong experience working with Tax Technology / Direct Tax environments.
  • ### Experience with Oracle TRCS or similar Tax Technology solutions preferred.
  • ### Experience with Oracle Cloud Financials is an advantage.
  • ### Understanding of corporate income tax, tax provision, transfer pricing, and tax data processes.
  • ### Experience translating business needs into product requirements, user stories, roadmaps, and prioritized backlogs.
  • ### Experience managing products or technology solutions through discovery, development, UAT, launch, adoption, and continuous improvement.
  • ### Strong understanding of data, analytics, system integrations, and enterprise technology.
  • ### Experience working with global, cross-functional teams across Business, IT, Engineering, and Data.
  • ### Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.
  • ### Demonstrated ability to simplify complex business and technology problems and drive decisions.
  • ### Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Taxation, or a related field; CA/CPA or equivalent professional accounting qualification preferred.

job.title: Data Center Logistics III - Singapore
job.description:
Job Summary

The Data Center Logistics III role supports the efficient movement, storage, and management of materials, equipment, and customer shipments within the data center environment. This role is responsible for coordinating shipping and receiving activities, maintaining inventory accuracy, supporting operational teams and customers, and ensuring logistics processes are executed safely, accurately, and on time.

Working independently on day-to-day logistics activities, the role helps maintain operational readiness, supports customer requirements, and contributes to the overall efficiency of data center operations.

Responsibilities

Documentation & System Updates

  • Maintain accurate records and supporting documentation for inbound and outbound shipments, inventory transactions, and customer deliveries.
  • Update inventory management systems and databases to ensure shipment and stock information remains current and accurate.
  • Verify goods received against purchase orders and delivery documentation, escalating discrepancies when identified.
  • Support reporting activities related to inventory levels, shipment status, and logistics operations.
  • Ensure inventory and logistics records are maintained in accordance with operational standards and compliance requirements.

Shipping & Receiving

  • Receive goods delivered to the Data Center directly or through established site security processes.
  • Inspect received materials and verify shipment accuracy prior to acceptance.
  • Coordinate timely dispatch and delivery of materials, equipment, and customer shipments to the appropriate destination.
  • Obtain delivery confirmations and maintain accurate records of completed deliveries.
  • Utilize shipment tracking tools, dashboards, and operational systems to monitor inbound and outbound shipments.
  • Support warehouse organization and ensure materials are stored safely and efficiently.

Inventory Management

  • Maintain inventory accuracy through proper receiving, storage, allocation, and tracking processes.
  • Allocate inventory and materials to internal customers and operational teams as required.
  • Coordinate inventory transfers between sites and support material movement activities.
  • Maintain appropriate stock levels for operational and project requirements.
  • Assist with inventory counts, stock audits, and reconciliation activities.
  • Communicate inventory shortages, backorder timelines, and replenishment needs to relevant stakeholders.
  • Support spare parts and operational inventory management activities.

Problem Solving

  • Work with suppliers, Original Equipment Manufacturers (OEMs), logistics providers, and internal stakeholders to resolve shipment and inventory issues.
  • Communicate delivery schedules, inventory availability, and shipment status to customers and operational teams.
  • Investigate inventory discrepancies and logistics-related issues, escalating complex matters when required.
  • Contribute recommendations to improve logistics efficiency, inventory accuracy, and customer service.

Hazardous Materials

  • Follow established procedures for the safe handling, storage, and movement of hazardous materials.
  • Ensure hazardous materials are properly labelled, documented, and stored in accordance with regional regulatory requirements.
  • Support hazardous materials inventory management and compliance activities.
  • Escalate safety concerns and ensure compliance with all applicable site policies and procedures.

Equipment Management

  • Organize and maintain inventory records for stored, staged, and abandoned equipment.
  • Monitor aging shipments and coordinate resolution activities in accordance with established business processes.
  • Support tracking of software licenses, technology assets, and related inventory where applicable.
  • Maintain accurate equipment inventory records and support asset management processes.

Data Center Support

  • Support the delivery and removal of customer equipment within data center environments.
  • Assist with equipment preparation, packaging, and shipment activities in support of customer and operational requirements.
  • Support Smart Hands and operational teams with logistics-related requests.
  • Ensure materials and equipment are handled safely and in accordance with site procedures.

Collaboration

  • Work closely with Customer Operations, Critical Facilities, Security, and other operational teams to support business objectives.
  • Coordinate effectively with customers, vendors, suppliers, and internal stakeholders.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives that enhance inventory accuracy, operational efficiency, and customer experience.
  • Share knowledge and assist team members during periods of increased operational demand.

Qualifications

Education & Experience

  • At least a Higher Nitec / Diploma certification, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Typically requires 1–2 years of relevant experience in logistics, warehousing, inventory management, supply chain operations, or a related environment.
  • Experience supporting operations in a data center, technology, manufacturing, industrial, or mission-critical environment is an advantage.

Preferred Skills & Experience

  • Familiarity with inventory management systems, warehouse management systems (WMS), or shipment tracking tools.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to inventory accuracy.
  • Ability to organize, prioritize, and manage multiple logistics activities simultaneously.
  • Effective communication and customer service skills.
  • Understanding of shipping, receiving, inventory control, and material handling processes.
  • Regional hazardous materials certification preferred.

job.title: Graduate Engineer
job.description:
Company Overview

STACK Infrastructure builds, owns, and operates hyperscale and colocation data centers that power the world’s most ambitious technology companies. With a rapidly expanding footprint across APAC, STACK combines deep development expertise, flexible capital, and operational discipline to deliver critical digital infrastructure at scale.

Our clients include the largest hyperscale cloud platforms. We are building a regional platform defined by speed of delivery, power reliability, and long-term partnership — and we are assembling the team to lead that effort.

STACK Infrastructure is seeking motivated graduates in Engineering and Construction to join our Singapore team and support the development and delivery of data centre projects in Malaysia and across APAC.

This is a full-time opportunity for graduates who want to build a career in the data centre industry. You will gain practical exposure to the design, development, construction, commissioning and handover of mission-critical data centres, supported by experienced colleagues and a structured development approach.

During the selection process, we will assess your interests, strengths and technical background and place successful candidates into the area most suited to them.

Engineering pathway

Engineering graduates may be assigned to teams supporting:

  • Design management and coordination
  • Engineering solutions and technical reviews
  • Commissioning, testing and operational readiness
  • Project coordination, quality assurance and issue resolution

You will work with internal teams, consultants, contractors and vendors to help ensure that systems are designed, tested and ready for safe, reliable operation.

Construction pathway

Construction graduates may be assigned to the Delivery team, supporting the planning and execution of data centre construction projects.

You will gain hands-on exposure to site coordination, programme tracking, contractor management, safety, quality, risk management and project handover.

What you will do

  • Support project teams with technical coordination, documentation and reporting.
  • Participate in site inspections, meetings, testing activities and project walk-downs.
  • Assist with reviewing drawings, technical submissions, work packs, test plans and project records.
  • Help identify, track and resolve technical issues, defects and outstanding works.
  • Work closely with project managers, engineers, consultants, contractors and vendors.
  • Support safety, quality and operational-readiness requirements throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Take on increasing responsibility as your experience, skills and confidence develop.

What we are looking for

  • A recent graduate, or final-year student graduating soon, with a degree in Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management, Built Environment or a related discipline.
  • For the Engineering pathway, a background in Mechanical, Electrical, Civil, Controls, Mechatronics or a related engineering discipline is preferred.
  • Strong interest in data centres, critical infrastructure, engineering, construction or project delivery.
  • Practical aptitude, intellectual curiosity and a willingness to learn quickly.
  • Good analytical, problem-solving and organisational skills.
  • Strong teamwork and communication skills.
  • Ability to work effectively in a dynamic, site-based environment.
  • Good written and spoken English.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications; familiarity with Bluebeam, Microsoft Project or similar tools is advantageous.
  • Willingness to work primarily on project sites and travel within Singapore and occasionally across APAC where required.

STACK is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer.

This job description in no way states or implies that these are the only activities to be performed by the employee occupying this position. Employees will be required to follow any other job-related instructions and to perform any other job-related responsibilities requested by their manager.

job.title: Project Manager
job.description:
Who we are

Digital Edge is a trusted and forward-looking data center platform company, established to transform digital infrastructure in Asia. Backed by Stonepeak, a leading alternative investment firm specializing in infrastructure and real assets, Digital Edge has in excess of US$1.6 billion in committed equity capital with investors including some of the world’s largest institutional investors and sovereign wealth funds.

Digital Edge’s vision is to be the leading provider of sustainable, next generation digital infrastructure in Asia. Our mission is to build the foundation for the world’s digital future, helping organizations to grow sustainably and empowering populations they serve.

Founded in 2020, the company has grown rapidly across multiple markets in the region and currently provides data center and fiber services across Japan, South Korea, India, Indonesia, the Philippines, Malaysia and China. The Company now owns and operates 21 data centers with over 500 MW of critical IT load in service and under construction and development, with another 300 MW held for future development,

This role is an exciting opportunity to join our fast-growing team as we further expand our footprint across Asia.

Our values:

**

  • Respect: We embrace diversity and collaboration.
  • Innovation: We share ideas and solve problems.
  • Strive: We are driven and determined.
  • Excellence: We seek to deliver the best.
  • Responsibility: We do what’s right for our people and the planet.

What we need:

**

The Project Manager – Data Centre will own end-to-end delivery of data centre projects, from initial design and planning through engineering, procurement, construction, and final handover. This role requires a strong technical foundation in mission-critical infrastructure, excellent stakeholder management skills, and the ability to coordinate across design, engineering, sales, construction, and operations teams to deliver projects on time, within budget, and to Digital Edge's quality and uptime standards.

Key responsibilities

1. Design & Planning

**

  • Lead pre-construction planning, including site evaluation, feasibility studies, and capacity planning for new builds, retrofits, and expansions.
  • Collaborate with architects, MEP consultants, and design engineers to develop data center design packages (electrical, mechanical, cooling, fire/life safety, security).
  • Review and validate design documents against Tier III/IV standards, local codes, and Digital Edge's technical specifications.
  • Manage design reviews (30%/60%/90%/100%) and ensure timely sign-off from internal and external stakeholders.

2. Engineering Coordination

**

  • Act as the primary liaison between engineering consultants, MEP contractors, and internal technical teams.
  • Oversee value engineering exercises to balance cost, schedule, and performance/reliability requirements.
  • Ensure compliance with uptime, redundancy (N, N+1, 2N), and energy efficiency (PUE) targets.
  • Coordinate technical due diligence for new sites and colocation builds.

3. Sales & Customer Support

**

  • Partner with the sales and business development teams on customer-driven build-to-suit or custom deployment requirements.
  • Support pre-sales technical discussions, capacity commitments, and delivery timelines for prospective clients.
  • Translate customer requirements into scope, schedule, and budget inputs for project planning.
  • Participate in customer-facing project updates for colocation/wholesale clients during construction.

4. Execution & Delivery

**

  • Develop and maintain the master project schedule, budget, and risk register across all phases of the project lifecycle.
  • Manage general contractors, MEP contractors, and specialty vendors (generators, UPS, cooling, BMS/EPMS, fire suppression, security systems).
  • Conduct regular site walks, progress reviews, and quality inspections to ensure adherence to design intent and safety standards.
  • Track and report on project KPIs: schedule adherence, budget variance, safety incidents, and quality/punch-list closure.
  • Manage change orders, variations, and claims in coordination with procurement and finance.

5. Commissioning & Handover

**

  • Oversee Level 3/4/5 commissioning (Cx) activities in coordination with commissioning agents and operations teams.
  • Ensure integrated systems testing (IST) is completed and documented prior to go-live.
  • Lead the transition from construction to operations, including as-built documentation, O&M manuals, and training handover to facilities/operations teams.
  • Support punch-list closure and defect liability period (DLP) management post-handover.

6. Stakeholder & Vendor Management

**

  • Manage relationships with landlords, utility providers, local authorities, and permitting agencies.
  • Chair regular project meetings with internal stakeholders (design, engineering, operations, sales, finance) and external partners (contractors, consultants).
  • Prepare and present project status reports to senior leadership and, where relevant, to customers/investors.
  • Actively champion and comply with policies and procedures related to workplace health & safety, information security, environmental, quality, energy management systems, incident management, and applicable legal and regulatory requirements.

The successful candidate:

  • 12-15 years of project management experience, with a minimum of 5 years specifically in data centre design, construction, and delivery.
  • Demonstrated experience managing the full project lifecycle: design, planning, engineering coordination, sales support, execution, and delivery.
  • Prior experience with mission-critical facilities (data centres, semiconductor fabs, hospitals, or similar) strongly preferred.
  • Experience working with colocation/wholesale data centre providers or hyperscale customers is a plus.
  • Existing network within the data centre industry (contractors, MEP consultants, equipment vendors) is a strong advantage.

Technical Skills

**

  • Strong understanding of data centre electrical and mechanical systems (UPS, generators, switchgear, CRAC/CRAH, chillers, cooling towers, BMS/EPMS).
  • Familiarity with Uptime Institute Tier standards and/or TIA-942 guidelines.
  • Working knowledge of commissioning processes (Cx Levels 1–5) and integrated systems testing.

job.title: Senior Director, Organisational Resilience
job.description:
About the Role

As Senior Director, Organisational Resilience, you will be responsible for ensuring our business can anticipate, withstand, respond to, and recover from disruptive events. You will partner with senior leaders across the organisation to embed resilience into operational practices and provide confidence that critical services can be maintained during major incidents or crises.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Leading and enhancing Optus' Enterprise Crisis Management and Business Continuity frameworks.
  • Overseeing enterprise-wide Business Impact Analysis (BIA) activities and continuity planning.
  • Driving crisis and emergency management preparedness through simulations, exercises, and executive rehearsals.
  • Providing strategic resilience advice and leadership during significant incidents and crisis events.
  • Monitoring organisational resilience maturity and supporting compliance with regulatory obligations, including critical infrastructure requirements.
  • Building resilience capability through training, awareness, and continuous improvement programs.
  • Leading lessons-learned reviews and driving sustainable improvements following incidents and exercises.

What makes you perfect for the role:

You are a seasoned resilience leader who combines strategic thinking with strong operational execution. You have a proven ability to influence senior stakeholders, navigate complexity, and lead effectively in high-pressure environments.

You will bring:

  • 10–15+ years' experience in business continuity, crisis management, resilience, risk, or related disciplines within large, complex organisations.
  • Experience operating within regulated industries or critical infrastructure environments.
  • Deep knowledge of business continuity management, disaster recovery, risk management, and enterprise resilience frameworks.
  • Strong executive stakeholder management and facilitation capabilities
  • Demonstrated success leading crisis response activities and resilience programs.
  • A degree in Business, Risk Management, Engineering, Telecommunications, or a related discipline. Postgraduate qualifications are highly regarded.

What's in it for you?

  • Competitive remuneration and employee discounts. Make life easier (and more affordable) with $80 monthly credit and 25% off Optus products and unique shopping discounts with our retail partners.
  • Flexible working arrangements with opportunities to work three days in the office, two days remote or home.
  • Competitive leave policies, including additional 'Connected’ days to focus on culture, family, health, community, or whatever’s important to you.

  • Build meaningful connections through employee-led networks and diversity initiatives including Culture Connect, Elevate Women, Disability Network and Express Yourself (LGBTQIA+).

  • Implement structured knowledge representations and interchange formats, including JSON-LD, RDF-style triples, ontology-aligned schemas, and Google Open Knowledge Format where applicable, to support reusable and machine-readable enterprise knowledge assets.

  • Familiarity with Apache Spark (especially PySpark) and large-scale data processing concepts
  • Hands-on experience with at least one vector database, graph database, search platform, or knowledge-store technology, and familiarity with embeddings, semantic retrieval, metadata filtering, and access-controlled retrieval patterns.
  • Self-starter with strong problem-solving skills and a keen attention to detail
  • Able to work independently while collaborating effectively with senior engineers, architects, product owners, source-system teams, and business stakeholders to translate requirements into secure and maintainable knowledge-system components.
  • Strong documentation and communication skills
  • Working knowledge of AI knowledge-system concepts, including knowledge graphs, ontologies or schemas, Google Open Knowledge Format, vector databases, memory stores, embedding pipelines, retrieval evaluation, access control, CI/CD, and production support practices.

job.title: Software Engineering, Machine Learning
job.description:
Meta is seeking engineers to join our teams in building cutting-edge products that connect billions of people around the world. As a member of our team, you will have the opportunity to work on complex technical problems, build new features, and improve existing products across various platforms, including mobile devices and web applications. Our teams are constantly pushing the boundaries of user experience, and we're looking for individuals who can help us advance the way people connect globally. If you're interested in joining a world-class team of industry professionals and working on exciting projects that have a significant impact, we encourage you to apply.

Responsibilities

  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams (product, design, operations, infrastructure) to build innovative application experiences
  • Implement custom user interfaces using latest programming techniques and technologies
  • Develop reusable software components for interfacing with back-end platforms
  • Analyze and optimize code for quality, efficiency, and performance
  • Lead complex technical or product efforts and provide technical guidance to peers
  • Architect efficient and scalable systems that drive complex applications
  • Identify and resolve performance and scalability issues
  • Work on a variety of coding languages and technologies
  • Establish ownership of components, features, or systems with proven end-to-end understanding

Minimum Qualifications

  • Track record of setting technical direction for a team, driving consensus and successful cross-functional partnerships
  • Knowledge developing and debugging in C/C++ and Java, or experience with scripting languages such as Python, Perl, PHP, and/or shell scripts
  • Experience building and shipping high quality work and achieving high reliability
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, relevant technical field, or equivalent practical experience
  • Experience with scripting languages such as Python, Javascript or Hack
  • 6+ years of experience in software engineering or a relevant field. 3+ years of experience if you have a PhD
  • 2+ years of experience in one or more of the following areas: machine learning, recommendation systems, pattern recognition, data mining, artificial intelligence, or a related technical field
  • Experience improving quality through thoughtful code reviews, appropriate testing, proper rollout, monitoring, and proactive changes
  • Experience with developing machine learning models at scale from inception to business impact

Preferred Qualifications

  • Masters degree or PhD in Computer Science or another machine learning-related field
  • Exposure to architectural patterns of large scale software applications
  • Experience with scripting languages such as PyTorch and TensorFlow
  • Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
  • Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
  • Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies

Meta builds technologies that help people connect, find communities, and grow businesses. When Facebook launched in 2004, it changed the way people connect.
